classification.difficultyReason: Translate the bagging conditions into divisibility constraints, construct an exhaustive bounded candidate search, and filter exclusions. Recognise that three totals survive despite the question's singular wording.

content.prompt: Helena has a basket of chocolates. There are fewer than 500 chocolates in the basket. Helena knows that she can divide all of the chocolates into bags holding 2 each, 3 each or 6 each. She also knows that it is not possible to put them into bags of 4, 5, 9 or 10. If she tries to put 7 in each bag, there are 3 left over. How many chocolates are in Helena’s basket?

inlines.text: List multiples of 6 below 500 that leave remainder 3 when divided by 7, then apply the remaining divisibility tests.

answer.worked:
The number must be a multiple of 6. The first multiple of 6 that leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7 is 24. Adding 42 preserves both conditions.

The candidates below 500 are
$$24,66,108,150,192,234,276,318,360,402,444,486.$$
Removing multiples of 4 leaves
$$66,150,234,318,402,486.$$
Remove 150 because it is divisible by 5 and 10. Remove 234 and 486 because their digit sums are 9 and 18, so they are divisible by 9.

The remaining numbers are 66, 318 and 402. Each is even, has digit sum divisible by 3, has its last two digits not divisible by 4, does not end in 0 or 5, and has digit sum not divisible by 9.
$$\begin{aligned}66&=7\times9+3\\318&=7\times45+3\\402&=7\times57+3\end{aligned}$$
Therefore Helena could have 66, 318 or 402 chocolates; the conditions do not determine a unique number.
